items.headline: Ong Ye Kung warns 'unnecessary treatments' could push up healthcare costs
items.summary: Health Minister Ong Ye Kung said Singaporeans are entering old age with more savings, but warned that overtreatment risks driving up national healthcare spending unless care stays appropriate and evidence-based.

items.headline: Josephine Teo says social-media bans are not the goal, but platforms must meet child-safety rules
items.summary: Minister Josephine Teo told a child-safety forum that outright social-media bans are not Singapore's preferred approach, but platforms will be held to enforceable safety standards for young users.

items.headline: Gym operator behind several Anytime Fitness and BFT outlets charged over late CPF payments
items.summary: Watchtower Holdings, which runs a number of Anytime Fitness and BFT gyms in Singapore, is being charged over the late payment of CPF contributions to its employees.

items.headline: Car bursts into flames on the TPE, snarling expressway traffic
items.summary: A car was engulfed in flames on the Tampines Expressway, with the fire reaching vegetation under a viaduct and causing congestion before it was put out.

items.headline: Copycat 'E20' movement demands minister Nitin Gadkari quit over the ethanol-petrol mandate
items.summary: Emboldened by the Cockroach Janta Party, a copycat E20 Janta Party is demanding Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari resign over the 20% ethanol-in-petrol (E20) mandate that drivers say hurts mileage.

items.headline: Modi pushes his ministers onto Instagram as Gen-Z protests reshape India's politics
items.summary: After his first selfie-style Instagram video neared 400 million views, PM Modi directed ministers to build Instagram presence; the platform's India daily active users jumped about 16% to 531 million amid the Gen-Z protest wave.

items.headline: India's economy sends mixed signals as a weak monsoon and trade shocks bite
items.summary: Businesses are juggling the Middle East war and US tariff threats while monsoon rains run well below normal, with slow government spending and fewer new projects clouding the growth outlook.

items.headline: India's $32 billion forex drive has yet to lift the rupee
items.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said banks have drawn about $32 billion under measures to attract foreign inflows, but the rupee has yet to strengthen much as war and trade uncertainty weigh on sentiment.

items.headline: Bank of England holds rates at 3.75% as three policymakers push for a hike
items.summary: The MPC voted 6-3 to hold at 3.75%, with Greene, Pill and Mann seeking a quarter-point rise; the hold followed a fall in headline inflation to 2.6% in June, a 15-month low.

items.headline: UK public services face a £24 billion squeeze this parliament, NIESR warns
items.summary: NIESR said higher energy prices and stubborn inflation will erode departmental budgets by about £24 billion over the current parliament, tightening the fiscal bind facing PM Andy Burnham.

items.headline: Only six of Burnham's cabinet would survive an election against Reform, poll finds
items.summary: Modelling by More in Common suggests just six of Andy Burnham's cabinet would keep their seats if an election were held now, with 12 losing to Reform UK.

items.headline: Shell posts its best quarterly profit in four years as the Iran war lifts energy prices
items.summary: Shell reported its strongest quarterly earnings in four years, helped by higher oil and gas prices driven by the Middle East conflict, as the London-listed major gained from disrupted supplies.

items.headline: Russian strikes kill at least eight across Ukraine and reach Lviv, forcing Poland to scramble jets
items.summary: Russian air strikes killed at least eight a day after Zelensky warned of a 'massive' attack, hitting targets from Kyiv to Dnipro and as far west as Lviv, prompting Poland to scramble jets.

items.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least four in Gaza, including a child, despite the ceasefire
items.summary: An Israeli strike on a Khan Younis displacement camp killed a man and an eight-year-old child, among at least four deaths in a fresh ceasefire violation, as Cairo phase-two talks stalled.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia proposes a naval coalition to guard Gulf shipping as oil prices ease
items.summary: Saudi Arabia said more than a dozen countries back a proposed maritime alliance to protect shipping lanes threatened by Iran and its allies; Brent eased nearly 2% to about $89 a barrel.

items.headline: Trump's August 1 tariff deadline looms as the EU nears a deal and USMCA lapses
items.summary: With Trump's August 1 tariff deadline a day away, EU and US negotiators neared a framework setting 10% tariffs, while Washington declined to renew USMCA and imposed a 50% levy on some Canadian goods.

items.headline: Judge doubts the US ban on Anthropic's AI, calling the 'supply-chain risk' case unproven
items.summary: A federal judge said the Trump administration lacked evidence to label Anthropic a supply-chain risk, calling the claim that its criticism of the Defense Department warranted a ban 'really troubling.'

items.headline: Apple beats on a 22% jump in iPhone sales but slides on weak guidance
items.summary: Apple's fiscal Q3 revenue hit $109.42 billion on a 22% iPhone jump, topping estimates, but shares fell about 8% after hours on 9-11% current-quarter guidance, below expectations, citing supply constraints.

items.headline: Amazon's AWS grows 37%, its fastest since 2021, lifting the stock about 10%
items.summary: Amazon reported revenue of $200.61 billion and EPS of $5.75, well above estimates, as AWS grew 37% year over year; the stock jumped more than 10% after hours with capex guided toward $220 billion.

items.headline: Reddit beats on earnings but sinks on fears of falling Google search traffic
items.summary: Reddit topped revenue and profit estimates and guided above expectations, yet fell more than 7% after hours as investors worried about a decline in search-referral traffic from Google.

items.headline: Wall Street rebounds as the Dow jumps 614 points after the Fed-day selloff
items.summary: US stocks recovered, with the Dow up 613.92 points (1.2%) to 52,208.06, the S&P 500 up 1.7% to 7,437.64 and the Nasdaq up 2.8% to 25,122.18, aided by cooling oil and strong Big Tech earnings.

items.headline: Coinbase falls after posting a third straight quarterly loss
items.summary: Coinbase slid more than 5% after reporting a loss of $359.5 million, or $1.36 a share, for the June quarter versus a $1.43 billion profit a year earlier, on revenue of $1.2 billion that missed estimates.

items.headline: Oil slips about 2% as Saudi Arabia floats a coalition to protect shipping
items.summary: Brent crude fell nearly 2% to about $89.03 a barrel after Saudi Arabia proposed a naval coalition to safeguard trade routes targeted by Iran and its allies, easing the war risk premium.

items.headline: Rivian rises after trimming its 2026 spending and narrowing losses
items.summary: Rivian gained nearly 2% after cutting 2026 capital spending to $1.7-$1.8 billion and narrowing its projected adjusted loss to $1.8-$2 billion as it began delivering a new midsize SUV.

items.headline: Eala rallies from 5-1 down to dethrone Fernandez and reach the Washington quarters
items.summary: Filipino 21-year-old Alexandra Eala overturned a 5-1 second-set deficit to beat defending champion and No. 7 seed Leylah Fernandez 6-2, 7-6(1) at the Mubadala DC Open.

items.headline: Cruz Hewitt, 17, lands his first top-100 win to set a Washington clash with de Minaur
items.summary: Cruz Hewitt, the 17-year-old son of Lleyton Hewitt, notched his first career win over an ATP top-100 player by beating Marcos Giron at the DC Open, setting up a meeting with top seed Alex de Minaur.

items.headline: Trent Rockets thrash Welsh Fire by nine wickets as Duckett hits 52 not out
items.summary: Trent Rockets cruised to a nine-wicket win over Welsh Fire in The Hundred at Cardiff, with Ben Duckett unbeaten on 52 and Tom Banton 31 not out.

items.headline: Horner's F1 return stays unresolved over the summer break as Cadillac denies links
items.summary: With F1 on its summer break, Christian Horner's route back remains open: Cadillac 'shut down' talk of hiring the ex-Red Bull boss and Renault says there are 'no discussions', while Horner pursues a team stake via BYD.

items.headline: Landmark satellite test confirms Einstein's 'frame-dragging' to one part in a thousand
items.summary: An international team combining LARES-2, LAGEOS and NASA's GRACE made the most precise measurement yet of frame-dragging, confirming general relativity to about one part in a thousand.

items.headline: NASA fuels its Roman Space Telescope for a late-August sky-mapping launch
items.summary: NASA loaded 290 gallons of hydrazine into the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope at Kennedy Space Center, keeping it on track for an Aug. 30 launch on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy.

items.headline: Euclid telescope uncovers 31 of the earliest quasars ever seen
items.summary: ESA's Euclid space telescope documented 31 of the oldest quasars on record, including two dating to when the universe was only about 5% of its current age.

items.headline: Immune cells in the blood drive brain ageing, and blocking them restores memory in mice
items.summary: A study reported in Nature found certain blood immune cells accelerate brain ageing, and that blocking their action improved memory in aged mice.

fun_fact.headline: The most remote spot in the ocean is Point Nemo in the South Pacific
fun_fact.body: The most remote place in the ocean, Point Nemo in the South Pacific, lies roughly 2,700 km from the nearest land in every direction. When the ISS passes overhead (about 400 km up), the astronauts aboard are often the closest humans; space agencies use the surrounding 'spacecraft cemetery' waters to ditch defunct satellites and stations.

puzzle.title: The Bookworm
puzzle.body: Three encyclopedia volumes (I, II, III) stand in order on a shelf, spines out, Volume I on the left. Each page block is 30 mm thick; each cover is 2 mm. A bookworm eats in a straight line from page 1 of Volume I to the last page of Volume III. How much paper and cover does it chew through?
puzzle.approach: Picture exactly where page 1 of Volume I and the last page of Volume III sit once the books are shelved in order.
puzzle.answer: 38 mm. Page 1 of Volume I faces Volume II, and the last page of Volume III also faces Volume II, so the worm passes only through Volume I's front cover (2), all of Volume II (34) and Volume III's back cover (2) = 38 mm, skipping the pages of Volumes I and III.

word_puzzle.title: The T Party
word_puzzle.body: Spelling Bee. Centre letter T; outer letters A, D, E, I, N, P. Make 4+ letter words that all use T; letters may repeat. Find the pangram using all seven letters.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must contain the centre letter T; the pangram uses all seven letters.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangram: PAINTED. Others include ADAPT, ADEPT, ANTE, ANTED, ATTAIN, DATE, DATED, DENT, DETAIN, EDIT, INAPT, INEPT, NEAT, PAINT, TAINT, TAPE, TAPED, TEPID, TIDE, TINT, TITAN.
